mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) accompanied by a decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate weakening labor market conditions, which typically precede a bearish S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by more than 0.2 percentage points while PAYEMS decreases over the next quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in comparison to historical labor market weakness periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a demand-supply misalignment that drives a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% while INDPRO falls by > 10% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when demand is strong and supply is weak (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over two consecutive quarters signals supply-side weakness that is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative during INDPRO contractions (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, the discount rate is expected to normalize, supporting equity valuation expansion and a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during comparable normalization periods (IC > 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment (UNRATE) without a corresponding drop in payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests a labor market correction that predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% while PAYEMS remains above 150K
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when labor market adjustments are present (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer confidence (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but implied by HOUST) and stable industrial production (INDPRO) indicate a resilient demand environment that is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when demand indicators are stable (IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and resource availability proxies (none directly available, so using INDPRO as stand-in) suggests supply constraints that drive a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not turn negative during sustained INDPRO declines (IC > 0.05).
